audit.whatIsWrong: The two layers disagreed on all seven rows: full read Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill/Fizz/Skill/Fizz, content read Fizz/Fizz/Fizz/Fizz/Karma/Fizz/Karma. The content layer also handed Fizz levels 1 and 2, which his kit cannot support.
audit.why: At levels 1-2 Fizz has only Urchin Strike, a 550-range dash, against Karma's 950 Q with Mantra already available — nothing there dodges her poke. Playful / Trickster arrives at level 3 and is the ability that flips the lane, at 16s rank 1 down to 8s rank 5. Level 6 is a genuine skill row (Chum the Waters at 120s against a Mantra she has had since level 1) and both layers' own prose already called it a coinflip. The late row goes to Karma on the same reasoning both layers' prose already gives: his burst is single-target while Mantra-E covers a whole side.
audit.corrected: Both layers now read Karma/Karma/Fizz/Fizz/Skill/Fizz/Karma, with the whys on every moved row rewritten to match.
sources: brief.enemyKit Fizz Q range 550, E cd 16/14/12/10/8 range 400
brief.ownerKit Karma Q range 950, R available at level 1

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[4].why read 'No new ult — your 6 is a Mantra rank... press the early lead before scaling lanes wake up' while the row was marked Fizz, and no spike named a cooldown.
audit.why: Chum the Waters is 120/100/80s and throws from 1300 range — far outside his 550 dash, so distance from Fizz is not safety. Karma's Mantra has been available since level 1, which is exactly why level 6 is an even exchange rather than his spike.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why, phases[5].why and breakdown.cooldowns now state the 120s, 1300-range ult and the first-item spike.
sources: brief.ownerKit Karma R text 'available at level 1'

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns held no digit (lint COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT), and the brief's missingInteraction — that Fizz's combo opens with an auto-attack reset — appeared nowhere on the page.
audit.why: Playful / Trickster is 16/14/12/10/8s at 400 range and makes him untargetable for the hop, so a Q or W spent into it is simply lost. Seastone Trident empowers his next attack on a 7/6/5/4/3s cooldown, so the attack wind-up is the tell rather than any cast animation. Fizz's passive also takes a flat amount of reduced damage from all sources, which is why chip poke does less to him than the numbers suggest.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns, tradeGood, tradeBad, dosFull[0].d, dosFull[1].d and report[5].t now carry the real numbers, the untargetable window, the wind-up tell and the flat damage reduction.

edits.before: This phase belongs to Fizz — his Playful/Trickster dash makes him untargetable through your poke, and the follow-up Urchin Strike plus autos lets him all-in you almost risk-free at levels 3 through 5. Play passively, ward for jungler assistance, and don't try to out-trade him in melee range since his kit is built to punish exactly that. Your best tool here is disengaging and denying easy CS rather than contesting trades directly. Expect to concede early lane priority and look to stabilize once your kit comes online.
edits.after: Levels 1-2 are yours — he holds only a 550-range Urchin Strike — but from 3 the phase belongs to Fizz: Playful/Trickster makes him untargetable through your poke, and the follow-up Urchin Strike plus autos lets him all-in you almost risk-free through level 5. Play passively from there, ward for jungler assistance, and don't try to out-trade him in melee range since his kit is built to punish exactly that. Your best tool is disengaging and denying easy CS rather than contesting trades. Expect to concede priority and stabilize on the plates you banked.

notes:
CHART: the two layers disagreed on all seven rows (full Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill/Fizz/Skill/Fizz against content Fizz/Fizz/Fizz/Fizz/Karma/Fizz/Karma). Both now read Karma/Karma/Fizz/Fizz/Skill/Fizz/Karma. Rows 0, 1 and 4 are matched full+content pairs; rows 2, 3, 5 and 6 are full-side edits where the content layer already held the target value.

CONFIDENCE: rows 0-3 and 5 are firmly grounded — Fizz has only a 550-range dash before Playful / Trickster arrives at level 3, and that hop is what flips the lane. Rows 4 and 6 I marked Medium: the kit does not settle them on its own, and I resolved each toward what BOTH layers' existing prose already argued (level 6 is a coinflip; Karma out-values single-target burst in a grouped fight). I did not invent a new verdict for either — if the user disagrees with row 6 in particular, it is the one to revisit.

NEW FACT ADDED: Fizz's passive takes a flat amount of reduced damage from all sources. Karma's whole pattern here is chip poke, so that flat reduction is directly relevant and appeared nowhere on the page.

missingInteraction landed: Seastone Trident's attack wind-up is the burst tell, written into dosFull[1].d where the bled tradeGood used to sit.

SuspectNames: wants.foe[2] 'Land Chum the Waters' is the correct name — false positive.

SCOPE: two report[] edits only (report[0].t, report[5].t). report[1].t and report[3].t still carry the old winCon / tradeGood / tradeBad strings and will read stale against the rewrites.

UNVERIFIED, left alone: whether Chum the Waters' knockup can be cleansed or is affected by tenacity, and whether Karma's Focused Resolve tether persists while Fizz is untargetable in Playful / Trickster. Neither is in Riot's text — the second is the single most useful unknown in this matchup and worth a decision from the user.
